question.text: Chapter 9 distinguishes Angel vs VC at the metric level. An Angel looks at team + CAC/CLV; a VC additionally looks at which revenue-consistency metric?

answer.text: Monthly Run Rate (MRR) or Annual Run Rate (ARR) — to gauge consistency and sustainability of revenue.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 says: 'Venture capital investors look at metrics like Monthly Run Rate (MRR) or Annual Run Rate (ARR), to gauge the consistency and sustainability of revenue generated by the investee companies.' MRR/ARR is the workbook's named VC-stage revenue-consistency metric, contrasted with the angel stage's focus on team/CAC/CLV. The Trap: Option B (EBITDA/DSCR) is a mature-business / debt-fund metric. Option C (EV/BV) is a banking-sector valuation measure. Option D (Altman Z) is a bankruptcy-prediction score for distressed investing, not growth-stage VC. Note: Use only the workbook's framing — VC investors use MRR/ARR for revenue consistency and sustainability — without adding term-sheet drafting prescriptions.
